subject: Request: Bridge affirmation & evidence roadmap for SOC 2 post-report gap
messages:
From: Maya Gonzales <m.gonzales@atlashealth.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 7 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: Bridge affirmation & evidence roadmap for SOC 2 post-report gap

Hi Logan,

Thanks again for the SOC 2 Type II we received yesterday. Our security review flagged a gap between the report period end (2025-09-30) and our procurement cutoff for go-live (current date). We need a short bridge affirmation letter that:

- Confirms controls in effect since 2025-10-01 through today (2026-11-07)
- Documents any material control changes or incidents in that window
- Provides an evidence plan (what we can expect to receive and when) so our Risk & Compliance team can close the procurement checklist

Can you confirm whether Redwood can provide a bridge letter (signed) plus supporting artifacts (system change log, incident summary, and a proposed evidence delivery schedule) within two weeks? If you have a template or examples, please share.

Also copying our procurement mailbox (procurement@atlashealth.com) to keep timelines visible.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — we have a security review meeting on 2026-11-20.

Best,
Maya Gonzales
Senior Security Analyst
Atlas Health

Hi Maya —

Thanks for the note and congrats on getting through the initial review. We can absolutely provide a signed bridge affirmation and an evidence roadmap. Proposed plan here:

1) Bridge affirmation letter (one-page) confirming that the controls tested in the 2025-09-30 SOC 2 Type II report remained in effect and were not materially changed through 2026-11-07, except where noted in the attached change log.
2) Supporting artifacts to be provided on a staged schedule:
   - Day 3: System change log extract (2025-10-01 — 2026-11-07) (CSV)
   - Day 5: Incident summary (all incidents with customer impact or control relevance) (PDF)
   - Day 7: Configuration snapshot & encryption key management note (PDF)
   - Day 10: Final signed bridge letter (PDF) and consolidated evidence folder (Drive link)

We will also include a short engineer attestation for any significant control changes. If DocuSign is required for procurement, we can route the bridge letter through DocuSign — I added an initial sign flow link in the related links.

Attachments I plan to include in the first wave: Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_20250930.pdf (you already have it), syschange-log-202510-202611.csv (sample extract), and a draft bridge-evidence-roadmap.xlsx showing the delivery schedule.

CCing Priya (Security Compliance) and Karthik (Legal) to confirm we’re aligned on wording and any legal language the procurement team expects. If you have template language your Risk team prefers, send it over and we’ll incorporate.

Thanks — we’ll aim to deliver the first two artifacts by 2026-11-12.

— Logan
Logan Wright
Account Executive, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Logan / Maya —

Thanks for the plan. A couple of compliance notes from our side:

- We should avoid language that implies a new attestation beyond the SOC 2 report; the bridge letter can state "to the best of management's knowledge" and list any documented changes.
- For the system change log, we will redact customer-specific PII in shared extracts. If Atlas needs unredacted artifacts, we can set up an NDA process — please confirm.
- Incident summary will include events categorized by severity and control impact; we won’t include raw logs, but can provide summaries and remediation timelines.

I’ll prepare a draft bridge template and the evidence roadmap workbook; Logan, I’ll upload day-3 artifacts to the Drive folder and notify Maya when ready.

— Priya
Head of Compliance
Redwood Inference
